litellm_entry.assessment: Best-supported public reconstruction: CircleCI invokes ci_cd/security_scans.sh, which installs an unpinned Trivy scanner via apt.
litellm_entry.boundary: Official prose retains attribution qualifiers; no original compromised CircleCI run logs or downloaded scanner hash independently reviewed. A GitHub Action is not established as LiteLLM specific ingress.

broader_chain.assessment: Trivy own GitHub Actions and distribution channels were compromised; that fact does not identify the integration mechanism used by a downstream project.

download_counts.boundary: Early author-reported result, not independently reproduced; full-window interpretation contradicted by later platform report.
Published platform download statistic, not unique victim count. No exact total or precise window endpoints asserted here.

quarantine_vs_deletion.boundary: Deletion by 16:00 differs from quarantine time. Do not use deletion as end of the active installation window. Its about-40-minute quarantine statement conflicts with the later PyPI report.

tags.assessment: Discoverer contemporaneous reporting says no matching tags/releases for the malicious PyPI versions; current disclosure page was edited March 30.
tags.boundary: No complete historical tag-event audit or archived immutable snapshot obtained; no present-day 404 used to prove historical nonexistence.

relation_to_current_versions: These findings concern malicious 1.82.7/1.82.8 in March. They do not establish poisoning of 1.100.0 or 1.101.0rc1.
